Deleting backups or shortening retention needs the approval of a second admin of the same scope (project admin, or cluster admin for the cluster). An approved request takes effect only after the deletion delay, counted from the request; until then any admin can cancel it. Deletions are requested from the backup catalog.
The backups are deleted for good once the delay has passed (object locks still apply). Any admin can cancel the request until then.

If this cluster is lost, nobody can decrypt its backups until the recovery kit of the active key is downloaded and confirmed (or the key is escrowed in a KMS). Download every share, give each to a different person, then confirm the kit by pasting enough shares back.

Backups are encrypted with their own key hierarchy, separate from the cluster's secrets. The recovery kit splits the key into shares: any threshold of them recovers it (e.g. 2 of 3), fewer reveal nothing. Each share can be downloaded only once. Disaster recovery from a fresh node asks for the kit (or the KMS) first.
Keep the DR info file (target locations and key generations, no secrets) with the kit: a fresh node needs both to rebuild the control plane.
A new key generation is created and used for new backups; existing backups stay readable with their generation's kit. The new generation has a new recovery kit that must be downloaded and confirmed.
The kit is split again: the previous shares stop counting and the new kit must be downloaded and confirmed.
Between 2 and 16 shares; at least 2 and at most all of them needed.
This share is shown only now and can't be downloaded again. It was saved as a text file; store it offline and hand it to its keeper before closing this dialog.
Paste the shares back (or load the saved text files) to prove the kit recovers the key. Needed:
Each share can be downloaded exactly once. It is saved as a text file and shown once; give it to its keeper and store it offline (print it, a safe, a password manager of that person).
Escrow the key in the KMS?
The key of this generation is additionally stored in the configured external KMS, so backups can be recovered with the KMS instead of the kit.

Control-plane backups are disabled in the cluster settings. Without them the cluster can't be rebuilt after losing its nodes.

The control plane backs up its own state: the Postgres database (continuously, for point-in-time recovery), OpenSearch (logs, audit, search) and etcd. Backups on the cluster's own storage don't survive the loss of the cluster; the external copy to off-cluster targets does.

If the whole cluster is lost, a fresh node rebuilds the control plane from the external copy. It needs the DR info file (target locations and key generations, no secrets), the access keys of the target and enough shares of the recovery kit (or the KMS the key is escrowed in). Keep the DR info file with the kit, outside the cluster, together with this release's agent binary (or the node installer, which takes --restore).
